title: Return by reference and return by address
recap: Returning a reference exposes an existing object instead of making a value copy. The referenced object must remain alive for every subsequent use by the caller.
Returning a reference to a local variable creates a dangling reference. Borrowing one of the caller's lvalue arguments is safe here because the caller retains those objects.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Practice return by reference and return by address.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement largerRef(first,second), returning an int reference to the larger caller-owned integer. On a tie return first. Do not return a local copy or a temporary. The caller may assign through the returned reference; tests check object identity, not just equal values.
hints: Select one of the reference parameters directly.
Use strict < so ties choose first.
Do not create a local result integer and return a reference to it.
